title: Persona pack manifest (persona.json)
description: Schema for personas/<id>/persona.json -- issue #70 (P2-1), design doc section 4.2. Both the Python and C# backends validate every enabled pack against this schema at startup and refuse to start on a violation (ADR-001 decision 1/2).

pronunciations.description: Issue #304: pack-level phonetic respelling lexicon -- e.g. {"Munchkins": "Munch-kins"} -- applied ONLY to the cascade pipeline's text-to-speech input text (CascadeProcessor/cascade_processor.py's `_speak`), never to the realtime model's own tool/item-name text, never to order/search data. Keys and values must be non-empty, trimmed strings. Optional: a pack with no brand words at pronunciation risk may omit this entirely or leave it {}.

logoTile.description: Issue #164 B2: when true, the shared hero renders `assets.logo` on a white rounded tile (an original's treatment for its opaque-background PNG logo) instead of a bare ``. Omit/false for a transparent-background SVG logo that needs no tile.

badge.description: Issue #164 A5: overrides the shared neutral 'Voice Ordering Demo' hero pill copy (e.g. a pack's own demo-crew phrasing). Omit to use the shared default.

description.description: Issue #164 A4: the persona's own hero sub-headline sentence (replaces the old app-level generic 'hero.subhead' i18n key).

callouts.description: Issue #164 A3: the three compact callout pills under the hero headline, in display order. `tone` selects which of the persona's own brand roles (theme.light.accents.primary/secondary/accent) the pill's gradient is drawn from -- NOT a literal color, so the shared component stays brand-free.

spotlight.description: Issue #164 A1/A2: the two spotlight cards beside the hero copy. The first card lists `rows` (label/value pairs, e.g. a featured-item name and a crew pick); the second instead pairs a `body` sentence with an `accent` pairing suggestion -- matching each original's two distinct card shapes.

icon.description: Pack-relative path under assets/ to this card's brand illustration (e.g. 'assets/spotlight-sample.svg').

tone.description: Issue #164 R4 (PR #167 round 1 review): which of the persona's brand roles this row's value text is drawn from. Defaults to 'primary' when omitted, matching each original's per-row value coloring.

Issue #164 A2: which of the persona's brand roles the second ('body') spotlight card's border/wash/kicker draw from. Defaults to 'secondary' when omitted (the first, 'rows' card always uses 'primary' and doesn't need this field).

accentTone.description: Issue #164 R4 (PR #167 round 1 review): which of the persona's brand roles the second ('body') spotlight card's accent pairing-line text is drawn from, independent of `tone` (which only drives the card's border/wash/kicker). Defaults to the tone-derived mapping already used before this field existed, so a pack that omits it renders unchanged.

tint.description: Issue #164 A2: optional hex wash applied to this specific spotlight card's background (e.g. a pack's tinted beverage card). Omit for the shared neutral surface.

variant.description: Issue #164 C3/E4: 'plain' (default if omitted) is the mono session-token bar most originals used, which follows the page's light/dark mode. 'chips' is one original's colored pill-chip bar, which always stays on its light background regardless of page theme.

categoryIcons.description: Issue #164 E1: optional menu-category-name -> emoji/icon override, keyed by the category's exact `menuItems.json` name. Exists so a pack whose menu data is shared territory (issue #165's menu-data work) can restore its original category icons WITHOUT editing menuItems.json itself. Other packs instead set `icon` directly per-category in their own menuItems.json (personas/menu.schema.json already supports that) since they have no such collision risk.

textRoles.description: Issue #164 R2 (PR #167 round 1 review): optional per-slot override of which brand role a handful of shared text elements draw their color from. Every key is optional; an omitted key falls back to the shared default (badge=primary, countChip=secondary, footerTagline=secondary, footerExtra=secondary) so a pack that omits the block entirely renders unchanged.

themeMenuSurface.description: Issue #169 (Rick's PR #167 round 3 review, item N13): optional pack-level menu-card/header surface tokens, layered on top of the shared shadcn `surface` slots above. Every key is optional so a pack without this follow-up still validates and simply renders the shared neutral defaults app/frontend/src/index.css falls back to. The same key set is reused for both `light.menuSurface` and `dark.menuSurface` (same convention as `themeSurface`) even though a mode only ever sets a subset -- e.g. a persona may set only the two card backgrounds in `light` and only the title color plus the item card background in `dark`, matching its own reference design (cream cards/headers in light, a bold category title and dark item cards in dark).

themeSurface.description: Optional shadcn-style UI slot palette (issue #117, app/frontend/src/lib/personaTheme.ts::PersonaSurfaceTokens/PersonaSurfaceDarkTokens). These back the shared shadcn tokens (card/secondary/muted/accent/destructive/border/input/ring/chart-N) that app/frontend/src/index.css previously hard-coded to one persona's palette; every key is optional so a pack that omits `surface` still validates and simply renders the shared neutral defaults. The same key set is reused for both `light.surface` and `dark.surface` -- which subset a mode actually needs differs (e.g. `chart2`/`chart3` are dark-only overrides, `accent`/`chart4` are mode-invariant and only ever set once under `light.surface`), mirroring how `light`/`dark` already share one `themeTokens` shape for the base roles.

themeAccents.description: Optional extended brand accent palette (issue #80 F2, app/frontend/src/lib/personaTheme.ts::PersonaAccentPalette). Role-named, not brand-specific: hex colors so a persona's exact pre-theming shades carry over without HSL round-trip drift. Every key is optional so packs without a curated accent palette (or a dark-mode override of only some keys) still validate.

primaryDeep.description: Issue #164 R2 (PR #167 round 1 review): an optional deeper/darker shade of the primary role, distinct from `primaryStrong`, for text that needs more contrast than the plain primary hex but isn't the hover/pressed `primaryStrong` state. Defaults to `primaryHex` when omitted.

secondaryLight.description: Issue #164 R3 (PR #167 round 1 review): an optional lighter shade of the secondary role, used for pill/gradient accents that need a brighter tone than `secondaryStrong`. Defaults to `secondaryStrong` when omitted.
